      <p class="hero-tagline" style="text-align:justify;">
        I am an applied microeconomist working on health economics, labour economics, and econometrics. My job market paper applies language models to Danish corporate disclosures to construct a firm-level measure of employers' emphasis on worker well-being, and estimates its causal effect on worker health using population-wide administrative records. More broadly, my applied agenda examines how economic and social environments shape worker health, team production, and social preferences, drawing on data from administrative registers, professional sports leagues, and online platforms. These applied questions also motivate my methodological work, where I develop machine learning tools to study heterogeneous treatment effects and ordered outcomes.
